what: the twin: the same bodies, the same passes, the same analysis, with mbedTLS's tables computed into SRAM instead (make RAMTABLES=1, which is ST's shipped default)

victim.stack: X-CUBE-SBSFU v2.7.0, 2_Images_ExtFlash, ST's shipped crypto scheme SECBOOT_ECCDSA_WITH_AES128_CBC_SHA256, mbedTLS as the package ships it
victim.build: make RAMTABLES=1 - ST's default, tables in .bss
victim.flash_acr: as SBSFU leaves it at 80 MHz
victim.table: mbedTLS RT0, 1 KB, four-byte entries, in SRAM
victim.table_addr: SRAM; the flash latch does not apply

geometry.note: Scored at the flash vector's own geometry on purpose. A control has to fail at the attack's settings, not at settings chosen to make it fail.

attack.expect_note: no key: across-chunk spread falls to the instrument floor and the pairs stop resolving
attack.note: Byte-identical bodies to the flash vector, one documented #define apart. Across-chunk spread is 83.1 cycles with the tables in flash against 22.5 with them in SRAM, on an instrument floor of 18.5. Marked slow: a control pays for the whole 2**23 residual before it can say no, which is about five minutes, where the flash vector finds the key in fifteen seconds. `run.py --fast` skips it.

truth.note: ST's published demo key, ASCII OEM_KEY_COMPANY1, which is what their prebuild step generates for this project. tools/replay.py compares the recovered key against it; the recovery reaches it through fw.plain and never reads this field.
